answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top. The result is a 10-card deck with I on top, then five II, then four III. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom.’

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. The human has two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in their garrison and nine troops in supply, and takes 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents start on the Leader; three troops start in the garrison, nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing you skip the rest of Player Turns and cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the cards revealed for that Reveal turn, not the cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns are optional; ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase’; resolve Reveal boxes of just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue may be played first on your Agent turn; resources it grants before placing the Agent can pay that entry cost. Effects from the played Agent card or destination that occur after placement cannot pay that cost. One card lets you choose only one Agent icon and send one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: entry costs are paid before effects; the turn notes allow a legal Plot Intrigue first, while later card/destination gains cannot pay the same entry; ‘You choose only one Agent icon.’

answers.answer: You may deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from your garrison, so at most five in this scenario. At a non-Combat destination you cannot deploy units through the normal deployment rule. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruit from supply into garrison; at a Combat space deploy any or all recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate lets you recall a Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent on that space; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a Spy from a connected post when you send an Agent, to draw a card. You cannot use the same Spy for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though you may use two different Spies for those two effects on one placement. Choose Gather Intelligence immediately after placing the Agent, before receiving space or played-card effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence is decided immediately after placing and before effects; same Spy cannot serve both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; last unit removed means strength 0. Combat Intrigue is available to players with at least one unit in the Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not bar you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved in Combat have passed consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after all involved pass consecutively; cleanup returns troops to supply, resets markers, returns worms to bank.

answers.answer: In four-player play, two tied for first each receive the second reward; neither wins the Conflict nor takes its card. The other players compete for the third reward. In three-player play, the same tie gives each tied player the second reward, and no other reward is given; nobody takes the Conflict card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first each gain second; no one wins/takes the card; with four, exactly two tied first lets remaining players compete for third; with three or fewer no other rewards. ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward offers 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost again to take it again: pay 3 spice for one VP, or 6 spice for two VP, if able.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms’ doubles; location control and battle icons cannot double; may pay an optional reward cost a second time.

answers.answer: On winning and taking a Conflict card, check immediately for a matching battle icon among face-up Conflict or Objective cards in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the pair face down for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win, check other face-up Conflict or Objective cards; ‘must flip’ a matching pair for 1 VP; Endgame wild matches any icon.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses that VP, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus; keep it if Influence falls below 4, and gain it again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also takes the Alliance and gains its 1 VP; tying the holder does not take the Alliance, an opponent must rise higher. The Alliance VP follows the token and is lost by the former holder on transfer.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 Influence track bonus is retained; Alliance token and VP transfer only when another rises higher.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent during your Reveal turn before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it from different sources for one card and split one source across multiple cards. The Row refills to five after an acquisition, so you may buy the replacement immediately if you can afford it. Put acquired cards face up in your discard pile. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal-turn timing, pooling/splitting, five-card Row replacement, acquired card to face-up discard, unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: At an Agent-free Maker space, add 1 spice during Makers to any accumulated bonus spice; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there, including when choosing a worm option. Maker Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them; they are not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, no worm can be summoned to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; removing it permits summoning at any Conflict. A worm is placed directly in your Conflict quadrant and never in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers and Sandworms: bonus spice accumulates; Maker visit gains all; Hooks are not universal and are retained; Wall protects three locations; worm cannot be in garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, after the round, 10 or more VP by any player or an empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare total VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Game end: Endgame is triggered at end of round; Endgame Intrigues resolve first; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has two contracts face up on the board and the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The ten contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: 20 contracts, flip two and put 18 in bank; shuffle four additional cards into each deck; Shaddam option; contrasting-back ten are separate Rise of Ix set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank contract flipped face up. If none remain, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes when you visit a Maker space and gain its stated spice amount during that turn, counting all sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM—Taking contracts and Completing contracts state the icon behavior and the three completion conditions.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there this turn, wait until a future turn; you had to hold it when you sent the Agent. Upon completion announce it, gain its listed rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: contract acquired after already visiting must wait; completion requires announcing, gaining rewards, and flipping it face down in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It takes the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to the humans, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective starts. First Player alternates only between humans; each round order is First Player, Rival, other human. The Rival takes Agent turns but never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival—Setup and Agent turns: one Rival, Ornithopter Objective, remaining Objectives to humans, first player alternates between humans; Rival immediately clockwise and never Reveals.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore if none, then immediately reveal another card and continue the Agent turn. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects; apply only the Hagal card effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination/reveal again; Place Spy cards do not place Agent; ignore normal costs/effects; empty or Reshuffle means reshuffle and continue.

answers.answer: Shuffle Objectives, remove any cards whose 1-3P or 4/6P marking does not match the player count, and give each player one at random. The player whose Objective shows the First Player marker takes that marker. Shaddam Corrino IV may only be used with the CHOAM Module, so cannot be chosen without it.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit Objective cards whose marking does not match player count, each draws one at random, marked Objective gets First Player; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, and water are treated as not limited; make any convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Sandworms also may be substituted as convenient. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return to it. Gains come from the bank and payments are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources/sandworms ‘not meant to be limited’; take gains from bank and return payments; recruitment says no more until troops return to supply.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card and then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round with Round Start.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference list phases; Phase 1 reveals Conflict then draws five; Recall returns Agents and passes First Player if no winner.

answers.answer: Yes. Board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and the automatic one Influence advance for a Faction space may be carried out in any order. No: you must meet the space requirement and pay its cost immediately before resolving effects, so the Influence from that visit cannot qualify you to enter it.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; gain space/card effects and Faction Influence; ‘You may carry out all these effects in any order.’

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can be paid and gained only once per turn; the exception is sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory, with exceptions including ‘may,’ optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon; a direct instruction to trash the card itself is mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play the card.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs and FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs specify once-per-turn rule, exceptions, and Intrigue requirements.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply when placement is needed, you may first recall one of your deployed Spies for no effect. If the effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, that type must be connected or the Spy cannot be placed.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: place at an unoccupied post; may recall one if none in supply; specific Agent icon must connect to post when specified.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate only bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Recalling a Spy requires playing a card for an Agent turn; you cannot use a Spy without that card. You may recall two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement, but cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on that placement.
answers.evidence: Spy rules: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says recall still requires playing an Agent-turn card and allows two different effects, not two Gather Intelligence uses.

answers.answer: The controller gains the location bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Control is obtained by winning the relevant Conflict, placing your Control marker and replacing an opponent's. On revealing a Conflict for a location already controlled, its controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict; no visit is needed.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: bonus on any visit; winning Conflict transfers control; reveal grants optional defensive troop from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player receives the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their rewards and Conflict card, but no further rewards are given. A tie for third in four-player play gets nothing. If three players tie for first, each receives the second reward and nobody wins/takes the card; in a four-player game no other rewards are given when three or more tie for first.
answers.evidence: Combat ties paragraph specifies second- and third-place ties and three-or-more tied for first.

answers.answer: In an ordinary three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive the first and second rewards; third receives nothing. This is also true when a Rival participates in two-player play: the Rival is a scoring third competitor, and the printed third reward is used only for a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with two or three players, ordinary first and second are rewarded; third gets nothing unless tied for second; two-player includes Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your Agent or Reveal turn, Combat Intrigues during Combat, and Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down separate from your deck and reveal only when playing; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile next to the Intrigue Deck. If that deck empties, shuffle its discard pile into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section states timing and storage/discard; FAQ Draw timing says reshuffle Intrigue discard if deck runs out.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, not an Intrigue unless specified; it cannot choose a card in play or in your discard pile. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets gives one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Trashing; and Secrets board-space entry specify hand source, Intrigue trash icon, and random steal from opponents with 4+.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing section and FAQ Victory: trash targets/zones and destinations; ‘The Spice Must Flow’s acquire VP is retained if the card is later trashed.’

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once, at the moment you acquire that card, not when you later play it. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Persuasion left over at the end of your Reveal turn is lost, not carried forward.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; unused Persuasion never saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond may use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order. Clean Up ends their in-play status as the cards move to discard.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond clarifies eligible cards and order; Agent-turn/Reveal rules say Clean Up moves all cards to discard.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent you just placed, to your Leader; you may use it on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict back to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; and FAQ Combat and troops state retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect that grants two Influence must put both advances into one chosen Faction, not split them. A Faction-specific effect advances only that Faction. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated minimum.
answers.evidence: Influence special rule: free-choice gain two cannot choose different Factions; Faction-specific icons; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the Alliance holder loses Influence after being tied, a formerly tied opponent takes the token; where several opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which one receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more to take the Alliance, return it to the board. The former holder loses the token's 1 VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss: tied player takes it; former holder chooses among several; if nobody has 4+, return to board; VP follows token.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and can be used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue with an effect that applies at Reveal remains face up until then, is used at Reveal, and is then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing states all three cases.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: such Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first; if received as a winning reward they can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If final VP and all four listed resources remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: last tiebreaker is most recent Reveal turn; scores may exceed 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement, provided you held them when sending the Agent. Their completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with board-space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: all same-space contracts fulfilled with one placement; they are another Agent-turn effect and can resolve in any order; must hold when sending Agent.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one of those set-aside contracts instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the round; follow the printed Leader restriction.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: Sardaukar contracts do not start in possession; ability allows choosing them; Signet Ring restriction is immediate and lasts that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training-track space and remains on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Begin with the Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications give Feyd setup/end, Jessica setup side, and Reverend Mother Jessica flip-turn timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 even when gaining multiple Influence at once. It can count again after losing Influence and later moving up through 2; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications on Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor state each point.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is a Spice Trade space: draw a card and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise gain 2 Solari. It does not automatically advance a Faction. Dutiful Service is an Emperor space: gain 1 Emperor Influence, then take a CHOAM contract or gain 2 Solari. It does advance Emperor Influence because it explicitly lists it.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Accept Contract and Dutiful Service; note says Landsraad, City, Spice Trade are not Factions and no automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen is City, costs nothing, and is Combat; the visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while the controller separately gets 1 Solari. Fremkit is Fremen, costs nothing, and is Combat; it grants 1 Fremen Influence and a card draw. Research Station is City, costs 2 water, and is Combat; it recruits two troops and draws two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide lists these entries and their icons/costs/effects; its Combat column marks all three Combat.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers all bonus spice plus either 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers all bonus spice plus either 2 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, one sandworm. You still take all accumulated bonus spice when choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent; the Shield Wall still prevents summoning at protected Conflicts.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Deep Desert/Hagga Basin and Sandworm Reward Doubling/FAQ Hook rule.

answers.answer: Both options require City access, at least 2 Fremen Influence, and no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Sietch Tabr: choose between the two stated options; both have no resource cost and require 2+ Fremen.

answers.answer: Each visit costs 5 Solari. On your first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On later visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops. High Council is not a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—High Council lists first and subsequent visit effects and Landsraad icon; it is not marked Combat.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster and 6 Solari after anyone does; each player may take it only once per game. The new Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Swordmaster entry and Rival resource/Swordmaster rules.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad and requires 2+ Emperor Influence; it costs 3 Solari. Its effects allow discarding an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recalling one of your other Agents and drawing a card. It recalls an Agent other than the one placed this turn and does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Privilege lists icon, cost, requirement and effects; Faction Influence is only gained on Faction spaces or explicit effects.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It grants 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Shipping: 3 spice; 2+ Guild; 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not a Combat space: recruit two troops for free, or pay 2 Solari to also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose no payment for 2 Solari, or pay 1 spice for 4 Solari; its controller separately gains 1 Solari on the visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Spacing Guild, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is Combat. Desert Tactics is Fremen, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card; it is Combat. Sardaukar is Emperor, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops; it is not marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, and Sardaukar show all listed effects and Combat designations.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, costs nothing, draws an Intrigue, and gives 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, gains 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws a card, and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, costs nothing, and gains 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes each affected opponent move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ clarifications for False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate ruling states restrictions and end-of-next-Reveal deadline.

answers.answer: The standard Rival receives four cubes on the bottom of the Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and put it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival scores and can win; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup gives components and says Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame like a human.

answers.answer: As soon as its counted resources reach its printed Swordmaster value, the Rival spends that many and takes its third Agent, usable this round. Resources count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water equally; spend in order Solari, spice, Intrigue, water, and keep leftovers. The Agent is available immediately in the current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster describes threshold, resource count/order, leftovers, and current-round use.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, it spends each such set for 1 VP. It cannot combine different resources into a mixed set of seven for a VP; the thresholds are separate resource sets.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster lists the four separate exact sets spent for 1 VP.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence; ties go to the leftmost Faction in its priority list. Like a human, it gains the VP at 2 Influence and Alliance VP while holding an Alliance, but it does not receive the resource/track bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster and Agent turns specify human-like VP/Alliance, no 4-Influence resource bonus, priority choice, and numbered icon meaning.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card the Rival selects only the destination matching current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal a new card rather than using the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract or Shipping, and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies or Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination selection rules and occupancy behavior.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional bonus requiring 2+ Influence is simply omitted if unmet; it never prevents Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat deployment; lack of 2+ bonus never prevents placing Agent.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes lists unrestricted post choice, all occupied case, third Spy Scheme, and no Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those troops too. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore its placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes and Agent turns specify same-turn Scheme troops and Place Spy continuation.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival always collects all accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none, it takes the base amount (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert); without Hooks it takes base spice. A protected Conflict prevents summoning; then it takes base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: collects all bonus spice, uses Hooks/worms only where permitted, otherwise takes listed base spice.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords as strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window, so they can respond afterward. A Rival with no deployed unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat explicitly sets timing, swords, Reshuffle behavior, human Intrigue window afterward, and unit prerequisite.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival receives normal control bonuses, defensive troops from supply, battle-icon VP, and doubled Conflict rewards with one or more sandworms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP when it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; with CHOAM a contract reward instead gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat states control, defensive troop, battle icons, doubled rewards, optional VP, and contract handling.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce your Combat strength and set your marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed during the turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength sections give timing, updates, and >20 marker procedure.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns. Merely revealing the Signet Ring does not activate it. Card text can override the game's usual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader ability note: Signet Ring ability activates when played on an Agent turn, not merely revealed; Overview says cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It does not inherently perform Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate no-card recall choices with their own conditions.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts distinguishes card Recall Spy icon from the separate Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence recalls.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot choose an Intrigue unless specified; it does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing and Discarding rules specify the separate Intrigue trash icon and ordinary discard limitation.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling lets you repeat the reward's one-Influence choice, so the two gains may go to the same Faction or different Factions. A single effect granting two free-choice Influence requires both gains to go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm doubling example allows 2 Influence with the same or two different Factions; Influence rule says a single gain-two choice cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn: the Rival follows its own House Hagal Signet Ring effect on its Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Hagal effects are applied on Rival Agent turns and it never Reveals.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival one token from the bank if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no additional token. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks it is ignored, and if the Wall is already gone there is no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table lists each stated state and result.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing, and is not a Combat space. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; also, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one selected at random to you.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Secrets entry and Intrigue rules distinguish deck draw from random opponent steal.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade, costs nothing, and is a Combat space. The visitor gets 1 base spice plus all bonus spice. Its controller separately gains 1 spice; if the visitor controls it, that same player receives both effects.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Basin: visitor gains base plus bonus and controller gains 1 spice; controlled-location note says both effects apply even if same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from previous rounds. Then each player draws five cards to form a hand. Thus the Conflict reveal precedes each player's five-card draw.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: reveal Conflict and place it on top of remaining prior Conflict cards; then each player draws five.

answers.answer: Place each human's cube at the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks; put one Alliance token on each Faction track. No human starts with an Alliance. The Shield Wall token starts in the marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is present initially.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks, Wall below Refinery, each cube at bottom; normal setup assigns no Maker Hooks, and no Alliance is assigned to a player.

answers.answer: In three- or four-player play the First Player goes first and players proceed clockwise; after someone Reveals, that player skips the rest of Player Turns, while others continue until all have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and goes clockwise. Each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards before passing or yielding.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 turn order and ending condition; Combat Intrigue starts First Player clockwise, and each eligible player may play any number or pass.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are: Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, then Clean Up. Reveal-box effects need not follow card order; resolve them in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists three steps and says Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's ten-card starting deck and place it face down to the left of the Leader. Without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards before shuffling the Intrigue and Imperium decks; each deck stays face down, and deal five Imperium cards face up into the Row. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks beside the Row. Set the Combat marker at 0; put three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers in the player's supply, with the four Influence cubes on the bottom Faction track spaces.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4, 6 and Initial card states give deck/Row/Reserve prep, markers and components.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion can acquire cards from the five-card Imperium Row or Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow from the Reserve. The cost is shown at the card's top right. These ordinary Persuasion purchases are made during Reveal, not Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards states eligible Row and Reserve cards, top-right cost, and Reveal-turn timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when legal placement/recall exists. Shield Wall removal is also optional: the detonation icon says you may remove it. Once removed it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies says ordinary placement and recalls are optional; Shield Wall section says may remove and it cannot return.

answers.answer: Normally the destination's upper-left Agent icon must match one Agent icon on the card you play. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City access send an Agent there; the card still needs a matching icon. If the card has a Spy Agent icon, it can send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn requires matching card icon; Special Rules says connected Spy alone does not grant all cards Spy access; Spy Agent icon provides connected-space access.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources gained only after placement from the played Agent card or destination cannot pay that same cost. You must pay the cost before resolving destination or Agent-card effects.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 entry-cost timing explicitly permits pre-placement Plot resources and excludes gains after placement.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, even after both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Proceed to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 two-player rule states continuation through Rival Agents after human Reveals and that Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, they may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict, without visiting that location with an Agent. After all Combat rewards, return troops to supply, return worms to bank, and reset all Combat markers to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive troop bonus; Phase 3 Combat cleanup resets markers, returns troops and sandworms.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve that played card's Agent box, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile, nor simply move an Agent already on the board; you place an Agent from your Leader. (A recall effect can separately return another Agent.)
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand and send Agent from Leader; use Agent box; recalled Agents are specifically other Agents.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot delay it by resolving the board-space effects first. The general freedom to order effects does not postpone the restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam says Emperor of the Known Universe restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send an Agent.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths, first, second, and third place each receive the corresponding printed reward. Fourth place receives no reward. The player with highest strength wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in four players first, second, third can receive rewards; highest strength wins and takes card; 0 strength gets no reward.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader ‘(choose, or select at random)’.

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You cannot choose a card directly from your discard pile; if the deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw uses own deck, not a chosen discard card; empty deck means reshuffle discard and continue.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Do not remove it.
answers.evidence: Rival Setup: ‘Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.’

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human player. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: put all Maker Hooks tokens in common bank; a token later acquired moves onto that player's garrison.
